claim: The genus-two row of Neumann's polynomial low-genus classification applies to a plane curve with normalization A^1 and exactly two ordinary nodes, and yields a hyperelliptic quintic model.
inspection: Internal primary-source reading plus rendered-page inspection.

sources.title: Complex algebraic plane curves via their links at infinity
sources.author: Walter D. Neumann

inspected.content: Section8 explicitly classifies most general defining polynomials up to polynomial ambient automorphisms and affine target-value changes. The sole realizable genus-two row is hyperelliptic quintic; the degree-six cable row is not realizable.
Coefficient-computation explanation and explicit application to a singular one-node curve. The two-node corollary is derived in the present proof, not claimed to be separately stated here.
Corrected Lemma7.1: a reduced fibre with a knot at infinity has a good defining polynomial.
Corrected proof of Lemma7.1, via Suzuki, iterated-torus-knot fibreability, and corrected Theorem6.1.

applicability: The specialized exact order has squarefree conductor length four and codimension two; its quotient partition consists of two disjoint pairs.
Thus normalization A^1 has exactly two ordinary nodes and one place at infinity.
Corrected Lemma7.1 ensures regularity at infinity; smoothing two nodes changes Euler characteristic from -1 to -3 and gives a once-punctured smooth genus-two fibre.
The defining polynomial is therefore in Neumann's genus-two table; its singular two-node fibre has a degree-five polynomial with two double roots and one simple root.
Affine normalization then forces a common midpoint of the two node pairs.
not_assumed: The singular two-node fibre itself is not a regular fibre.
The table is not used merely as topological knot classification; its stated polynomial ambient-equivalence conclusion is essential.
No target automorphism varying algebraically over the parameter line is assumed.
The later conditional parametric-lines classification is not used.
